method: grep -rE 'unlink\(|write_text\(|write_bytes\(|open\([^)]*[\x27\"]w|shutil\.(copy|move)|\.rename\(|\.replace\(|truncate\(' over every test_*.py in intel/, then manually read each match's surrounding context (module-level path constants, tempfile usage, restore discipline, and whether restore is gated behind if __name__=="__main__"). Builds on and re-verifies the N-9B audit (intel/phase_n9/n9b_test_isolation_audit.json), which already found and fixed test_url_resolver.py/test_source_registry.py.

UNSAFE_CANONICAL_MUTATION_FOUND_AND_FIXE.root_cause: _restore_real_files() was only called inside main()'s try/finally, and main() only runs under `if __name__ == "__main__":` (i.e. `python3 file.py`). Under pytest, the test_* functions are collected and called directly -- main() never runs -- so the first test's _cleanup() snapshots the real canonical file (claims.json / hypotheses.json / intelligence_objects.json / statistical_evidence.json) and then unlinks it, and nothing ever restores it. A pytest run of any of these 6 files permanently deletes real production canonical data.
UNSAFE_CANONICAL_MUTATION_FOUND_AND_FIXE.fix_applied: PRIORITY 1 (true per-test path isolation via monkeypatched module path constants) was considered but rejected as the pragmatic choice: each of these 6 files' module-under-test (claim_model, hypothesis_model, intelligence_object, statistical_evidence) reads its canonical PATH constant once at import time and several already-passing tests call public API functions (new_claim/upsert_claim/load_claims etc.) that close over that constant internally, so swapping it mid-run for only some tests would require re-importing the module per test or passing an explicit path through every call site -- a larger, riskier change than this closure phase's scope, and not what the file's own existing manual-test-runner architecture (`tests = [...]` + `main()`) was built around. PRIORITY 2 (snapshot once at import -> run -> guaranteed restore) was applied instead, by adding `atexit.register(_restore_real_files)` immediately after `_restore_real_files` is defined, at module level (so it is registered the moment the module is imported, before any test runs, regardless of invocation style). This is the exact same pattern already used elsewhere in this repo (test_url_resolver.py, test_source_registry.py, test_live_result_guard.py, all fixed in N-9B for the identical bug class), so it introduces no new restore mechanism -- it extends an existing, proven one to the 6 files that were missed when N-9B's own fix for 4 of these same files was written gated-on-main() instead. main()'s try/finally call to _restore_real_files() was left in place unchanged (harmless, idempotent double-restore under `python3 file.py`); no shared helper module was created because `atexit.register(_restore_real_files)` is a single line added directly after each file's own existing _restore_real_files() definition, which is simpler than introducing a new intel/_test_support/ package for a one-line fix repeated 6 times.
verification: python3 -m pytest <each of the 6 files> -q individually: all pass, canonical file SHA-256 unchanged before/after (see o1f_before_snapshot.json canonical_file_sha256_before vs post-run hashes in the handback report).
python3 <each of the 6 files>.py individually: all pass (manual runner convention still works), canonical file SHA-256 unchanged before/after.

Failure-path check: a deliberate `assert False` was temporarily inserted into test_claim_model.py's test_upsert_and_load_roundtrip, run under both pytest and `python3 file.py` (both correctly reported the failure), confirming claims.json SHA-256 was identical before and after in both cases, then the deliberate failure was removed and the file restored to its real fix (git diff confirms only the atexit.register line was added, no leftover test code).

SAFE_ISOLATED_tempdir_or_own_tempfile_sc.note: Every write/unlink/rename target is under tempfile.mkdtemp()/tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()/tmp_path, or the test's own throwaway scratch path under its own tests/ dir (e.g. _atomic_publish_scratch/, _test_result_tmp.json, _test_site_as_file.tmp), guarded by try/finally or by being fully contained inside a `with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` block. Never a package-root canonical *.json path.

SAFE_READ_ONLY_source_text_assertion.note: The matched open(...,'w') substring appears only inside a string literal being asserted absent from production source code (e.g. assert 'open(DOCUMENTS_PATH, "w")' not in src) -- the test itself performs no file write. Re-verified from N-9B's identical finding.

MUTATES_BUT_SAFELY_ISOLATED_atexit_snaps.note: Already fixed in N-9B with the same atexit.register(restore) pattern applied to the 6 files above: snapshot taken at module import time (before any test runs), restore registered at interpreter exit, which fires regardless of pytest vs `python3 file.py` and on unhandled exceptions. Re-verified present and unchanged this phase, not re-modified.

SAFE_ISOLATED_no_mutation_pattern_match.note: No unlink/write_text/write_bytes/open(...,'w')/shutil.copy|move/.rename/.replace/truncate pattern found at all; these files are either SAFE_READ_ONLY (read canonical fixtures/corpora but never write) or fully SAFE_ISOLATED (synthetic in-memory fixtures with no filesystem interaction). Not individually re-read line-by-line in this phase given the absence of any matching pattern; see files_with_no_mutation_pattern... list above for the full enumeration.

honest_gap: The 103 SAFE_ISOLATED_no_mutation_pattern_match files were classified by absence of the grep pattern only, not by individually reading every one of the 103 files end-to-end -- a file that mutates a canonical path through an indirection the grep pattern does not catch (e.g. a helper function in the module under test, called with no literal 'w' mode or .unlink() token in the test file itself) would not be caught by this method. This is the same methodology N-9B used and is disclosed as a limitation there too; no evidence was found of such an indirect case during this phase's full regression run (step 10), which would have shown an unexpected canonical-file diff in `git status --short` between test batches if one existed.
